notes: Job TRANREPT (app/proc/TRANREPT.prc) step STEP05R, a DFSORT step, not a COBOL program: SORT FIELDS=(TRAN-CARD-NUM,A) with INCLUDE COND=(TRAN-PROC-DT,GE,PARM-START-DATE,AND,TRAN-PROC-DT,LE,PARM-END-DATE) over its SYMNAMES (TRAN-CARD-NUM 263,16,ZD; TRAN-PROC-DT 305,10,CH; 2022-01-01 .. 2022-07-06). DFSORTST.cbl is that step lowered by gitgalaxy/tools/cobol_to_java/det/dfsort.py (cobol_program(parse(SYSIN, SYMNAMES), 350, ['SORTIN']); test_sort_case_4268.py pins the file to that output) onto the COBOL SORT verb with an INPUT PROCEDURE (the INCLUDE) and an OUTPUT PROCEDURE; GnuCOBOL runs it (the oracle), the port is its det translation, and SORTOUT is compared record by record under CVTRA05Y. The lowering is the assumption (register F4, IBM z/OS DFSORT Application Programming Guide SC23-6878): the step has no EQUALS, so equal keys come out in an order DFSORT does not promise and the port stops by name on two equal keys of differing records; sortin.txt therefore holds one record per card (the 50 distinct TRAN-CARD-NUM of carddemo-trnrpt's transact.txt, the POSTTRAN output), shuffled (seed 4268), their TRAN-PROC-TS dates cycled over 2021-12-31, 2022-01-01, 2022-03-15, 2022-07-06, 2022-07-07 and 2022-07-18 so the INCLUDE keeps the first boundary and a middle date, the upper bound, and drops one on each side and the posting date. The key is a ZD (signed by value) field over digit data and the date compare is CH over digits and hyphens, where IBM's EBCDIC order and the oracle's byte order agree (collation, #4035: a CH key over letters is the det dfsort collation slice).
